purpose: Map macro blocks to each central bank's actual mandate/reaction function before translating them into rates and FX implications. This file does not change engine weights, thresholds, live data, or prior backtest results.
principles: Do not assume a universal macro-to-FX mapping across currencies.
Distinguish direct policy variables from indirect transmission variables.
Labour may enter policy directly, or mainly through wages/services inflation depending on mandate and reaction function.
Rates/front-end repricing remains the market confirmation layer between macro and FX.
No production weighting changes until PIT evidence supports them out of sample.

core_transmission: Labour -> Fed reaction -> front-end rates -> USD
Inflation -> Fed reaction -> front-end rates -> USD
FED.interpretation_rule: Labour deterioration can directly alter policy expectations even without first passing through wages or inflation, subject to the balance of risks on both sides of the mandate.

secondary_objectives: support general EU economic policies including employment, without prejudice to price stability
core_transmission: Labour -> wages -> services/domestic inflation -> ECB reaction -> front-end rates -> EUR
Inflation -> ECB reaction -> front-end rates -> EUR
ECB.interpretation_rule: Headline employment/unemployment should not automatically map one-for-one into EUR direction. Labour information is more policy-relevant when it changes wage pressure, services inflation, domestic inflation persistence or the medium-term inflation outlook.
ECB.testing_implication: EUR Labour standalone should remain diagnostic until PIT wage/services-inflation mediation is tested.

secondary_objectives: support government economic policy including growth and employment, subject to price stability
core_transmission: Labour tightness -> wages -> services/domestic inflation -> BoE reaction -> front-end rates -> GBP
Inflation persistence -> BoE reaction -> front-end rates -> GBP
BOE.interpretation_rule: Employment/unemployment matter, but wage growth, labour tightness and services inflation are usually the more direct monetary-policy bridge.

core_transmission: Labour/slack -> BoC reaction -> front-end rates -> CAD
Inflation persistence -> BoC reaction -> front-end rates -> CAD
BOC.interpretation_rule: Labour has direct policy relevance, but the inflation-control target remains the anchor; the balance between slack and inflation persistence matters.

core_transmission: Labour/full-employment gap -> RBA reaction -> cash-rate expectations -> AUD
Inflation -> RBA reaction -> cash-rate expectations -> AUD
RBA.interpretation_rule: Both price stability and sustained full employment should be evaluated directly; policy balances the two objectives under flexible inflation targeting.

core_transmission: Labour/economic slack -> inflation outlook -> RBNZ reaction -> front-end rates -> NZD
Inflation -> RBNZ reaction -> front-end rates -> NZD
RBNZ.interpretation_rule: Since the 2023 remit change, maximum sustainable employment is no longer a formal objective; employment matters mainly as a variable whose unnecessary volatility should be avoided and as information for inflation pressure/slack.

secondary_objectives: take due account of economic developments
core_transmission: Labour/economic activity -> inflation forecast -> SNB reaction -> rates/FX intervention -> CHF
Inflation forecast -> SNB reaction -> rates/FX intervention -> CHF
SNB.interpretation_rule: Labour should not map directly into CHF direction; the SNB prioritises price stability and explicitly uses both interest rates and the exchange rate to shape monetary conditions.

core_transmission: Labour tightness -> wages -> sustainable underlying inflation -> BoJ reaction -> JPY rates -> JPY
Inflation/wage cycle -> BoJ reaction -> JPY rates -> JPY
BOJ.interpretation_rule: Employment conditions matter mainly insofar as they support wage growth and a sustainable price-wage cycle consistent with the 2% price-stability target; headline labour alone should not be treated as a direct policy vote.

backtest_policy.required_next_test: Test reaction-function-aware labour channels out of sample: direct labour for dual-mandate banks versus mediated labour->wages/services inflation or slack->inflation channels for price-stability-primary banks.
